question:
Choose the word which is nearly opposite in meaning to the given word:-

Malevolent
solution:
The correct answer is 'Kindly'.
Key Points
  • The word ‘Malevolent’(adjective) means- "having or showing a desire to harm others". (बुरा चाहनेवाला या अनिष्ट करनेवाला; ईर्ष्यालु)
    • E.g: The central character is a malevolent witch out for revenge.
  • ​Let’s have a look at the meaning of the words that are given in the options:
    • Kindly(adjective)- “of a person having a character that is generous, helpful, and caring about other people”. (एक ऐसे व्यक्ति का चरित्र जो उदार, मददगार और अन्य लोगों की परवाह करने वाला हो)
    • Vacuous(adjective)- “showing a lack of intelligence or feeling”. (बुद्धि या भावनाओं की कमी; मूढ़; भावशून्य; विचारशून्य)
    • Ambivalent(adjective)- “having or showing a mixture of feelings or opinions about something or somebody”. (मिश्रित या मिली-जुली भावनाओं से युक्त; उभयमुख)
    • Primitive(adjective)- “very simple and not developed”. (अत्‍यंत साधारण और अविकसित)
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘Kindly’ is the correct antonym of the given bold word.

Additional Information

  • The antonyms of the given word 'Malevolent' are-  'Kindly', 'benevolent', 'good', 'amiable', 'liking', etc.
  • The synonyms of the given word 'Malevolent' are- 'malicious', 'hostile', 'bitter', 'vicious', etc.
  • Example of 'Malevolent' in a sentence: 
    • I could feel his malevolent gaze as I walked away.

question:

solution:

Key Points

  • It's will replace its.
  • It's is the short form of It is, whereas "its" shows possession of something or someone.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. if there is no error, select 'No error'.

During the summer months, there is shortage of power in much parts of the country.
options: in much parts of the country
solution:
The erroneous part is 'in much parts'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'in many parts' should be used instead of 'in much parts'.
  • 'Much' is used to describe mass nouns or non-count nouns like juice, rice, patience, and happiness.
  • When using 'much', the noun will always be singular; it cannot be plural.
  • 'Many' is used to describe count nouns or nouns that can be counted like books, ideas, leaves, and shoes. 
  • In the given sentence 'parts of the country' is countable.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct Sentence: During the summer months, there is shortage of power in many parts of the country.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहाँ 'in much parts' के स्थान पर 'in many parts' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • 'juice, rice, patience, and happiness' जैसे mass nouns या non-count nouns का वर्णन करने के लिए 'much' का उपयोग किया जाता है।
  • 'much' का प्रयोग करते समय noun सदैव singular होगी; यह plural नहीं हो सकता।
  • 'Many' का उपयोग count nouns या nouns का वर्णन करने के लिए किया जाता है जिन्हें books, ideas, leaves, and shoes की तरह गिना जा सकता है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में 'parts of the country' गणनीय है।
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“Please stand in a queue,” said the teacher to the students.
options: The teacher ordered the students stand in a queue.
The teacher said the students to please stand in a queue.
The teacher told the students to be stood in a queue.
The teacher requested the students to stand in a queue.
solution:
The correct answer is 'The teacher requested the students to stand in a queue.'

Key Points

  • While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow the given steps-
    • The conjunction 'to' should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”).
    • 'Said to' is changed into 'ordered/ requested/ advised/ forbade, etc.'
    • 'To' is followed by 'V1'.
    • At last line up the remaining part.
       

The final sentence- The teacher requested the students to stand in a queue.

Additional Information

  • An 'Imperative sentence' is a type of sentence that gives instructions or advice and expresses a command, an order, a direction, or a request.
  • It is also known as a jussive or a directive. Depending upon its delivery, an imperative sentence may end with an exclamation mark or a period.

question:
Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

An anthology of poems on childhood is being written by her.
options: She is writing an anthology of poems on childhood.
She has been writing an anthology of poems on childhood.
She has written an anthology of poems on childhood.
She will be written an anthology of poems on childhood.
solution:
The correct answer is 'She is writing an anthology of poems on childhood.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Present Continuous Tense and in Passive Voice.
  • The rule for changing a Present Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
    • Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
    • Structure: 
      • Subject + is/am/are + v1 + ing + object (Active Voice)
      • Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by Subject (Passive Voice) 
    • Example: 
      • Esha is singing a song. (Active Voice)
      • A song is being sung by Esha. (Passive Voice)
        ​

Correct Answer: She is writing an anthology of poems on childhood.

Additional Information    

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
    • Example: He reads a novel. (Active Voice)
                       A novel is read by him. (Passive Voice)​

Hinglish   

  • दिया गया वाक्य Present Continuous Tense और Passive Voice में है।
  • Present Continuous Tense को Active voice से Passive voice या Passive voice से Active voice में बदलने का नियम:
    • Object और Subject को एक दूसरे के साथ बदलें, यानी Active Voice का object, Passive Voice का subject बन जाती है।
    • Structure: 
      • Subject + is/am/are + v1 + ing + object (Active Voice)
      • Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by Subject (Passive Voice) 
    • Example: 
      • Esha is singing a song. (Active Voice)
      • A song is being sung by Esha. (Passive Voice)

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Several minutes had passed / before she returned / carry milk / for the dog.
options: Several minutes had passed
solution:
The erroneous part is "carry milk"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the usage of "carry" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "carrying"
  • In the given sentence, there are two clauses the main clause and the subordinate clause. In the subordinate clause, i.e. "before clause" "returned" is the main verb and a transitive verb and we know that after the transitive verb we always need to use an object. 
  • "carry" is a verb hence, we need to use a present participle form of this i.e. "carrying" so the main object will be "milk". "carrying" will tell about "milk".

So the correct sentence is- Several minutes had passed before she returned carrying milk for the dog.

question:
Choose an appropriate modal for the given sentence:

Last Saturday, Sangeetha confirmed that she ___________ help me in my project.
solution:
The correct answer is "would".

Key Points

  • We will apply "would" in this sentence because the sentence is trying to emphasize something.
  • Would is commonly used to indicate conditional mood and to describe the outcome of an imagined circumstance or event.
  • "Would" is a modal we use in formal situations or to enhance something.
    • Example: Your mother would approve of this picnic.
  • It is apparent from the above explanation that the modal "would" is correct for this sentence.
  • Therefore, the complete sentence is: Last Saturday, Sangeetha confirmed that she would help me with my project.

Additional Information

Let's know more about the modal:

  • Modal verbs are used to express a variety of fictitious circumstances, such as suggestions, capacities, or demands.
  • They are used in conjunction with a primary verb to subtly alter its meaning.
  • They can't necessarily be used on their own because they are auxiliary verbs.
  • Can, could, may, might, must, ought to, shall, should, would, and would not are some of the modal verbs.
    • Example: Can you do this? (referring to capability)
    • Example: You may go. (referring to permission)

question:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.
 

My family asked me to bring a dozen of fruits.
options: I was asked to bring a dozen fruits by my family.
They asked me to bring a dozen of fruits.
I am asked to bring a dozen of fruits.
My family is asking me to ring a dozen of fruits.
solution:
The Correct answer is 1 i.e. I was asked to bring a dozen fruits by my family.

Key-point

  • The given sentence is in an active voiceform hence we need to convert it into a passive voice form.
  • Following rules should be taken care of while changing a sentence into its passive form.
  • Find the subject and object of the active sentence and exchange it accordingly.
    • Like, the subject of the active sentence will become the object of the passive sentence and the object of the active sentence will convert into the subject of the passive sentence.
    • As the active voice sentence is in Simple past tense we will use the given structure to convert it into its passive voice form "STRUCTURE: Sub+V2+ Obj (active) changes to Sub+ was/were+ V3+ Obj".
    • Let's see the examples:
      • Everyone submitted the assignment on time. (active).
      • The assignment was submitted on time. (passive)
  • After following the above-mentioned steps we finally get -I was asked to bring a dozen fruits by my family

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The teacher said to the students, "Can you tell me what have you learned in geography class?"
options: The teacher told the students to tell him what they learned in geography class.
The teacher wanted the students to tell him what they learned in geography class.
The teacher asked the students if they could tell him what they had learned in geography class.
​The teacher asked the students what they can tell him what they had learned in geography class.
solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'The teacher asked the students if they could tell him what they had learned in geography class.'

 Key Points

  • The given sentence is an interrogative sentence in Direct Speech. As per the given directions, we have to change it into Indirect Speech.
  • The process of transformation is as follows:
  • The conjunction 'if' will be added and comma and inverted commas will be removed.
  • In the Indirect speech 'said to' will be changed into 'asked' because the reporting verb has an object, 'the students.'
  • The indirect speech will begin like 'The teacher asked the students if.'
  • Now we have to change the reported speech.
  • In the reported speech, the pronoun 'you' will be changed into 'they.'
  • The verb 'can' will be changed into 'could.' 
  • The pronoun 'me' will be changed into 'him.'
  • The present perfect tense 'have learned' will be changed to the past perfect tense 'had learned.'
  • Here, 'Can you tell me what you have learned in geography class' is in an interrogative sentence and will be changed into an assertive sentence i.e., 'they could tell him what they had learned in geography class.'
    Finally, the indirect speech is 'The teacher asked the students if they could tell him what they had learned in geography class.'
  • So, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct Sentence: The teacher asked the students if they could tell him what they had learned in geography class.

question:
Choose the appropriate tense to fill in the blank in the given sentence:

Mary _________ to a new school next term.
solution:
The correct answer is is going.

Key Points

  • "Is going"- in the given sentence the verb is in present continuous tense.
  • The present continuous tense is frequently used to refer to temporary situations or actions.
  • We can also state that, we employ the present continuous tense to describe an action or state that is currently occurring and will continue to occur until an unknown period in the future.
  • We also frequently employ the present continuous tense to refer to future events, particularly those that have been planned.
  • In order to make it clear that the present continuous tense is being used to allude to a future event rather than an event that is currently taking place, we frequently express this by using adverbs of time.
    • Example- We are celebrating their anniversary next week.
    • Example- Tina is going to Canada this summer.
  • The above sentence implies that Mary will go to a new school in future, that means it is a future event. Therefore, "is going" is the appropriate option among the other given options.

question:
Choose the correct passive construction of the sentence:

Someone has cut the telephone wires.
options: The telephone wires has been cut.
The telephone wires have been cut.
The telephone wires were found cut.
solution:
The correct answer is - The telephone wires have been cut.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in an active voice form, hence we need to convert it into a passive voice form.
  • We need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an assertive sentence.
  • Find the subject (someone) and object (the telephone wires) of the sentence and exchange their places. 
  • If the subject (someone) isn't clear, we don't need to add 'by + new object' in the passive voice form.
  • The given sentence is in the present perfect tense.
  • The passive verb form for present perfect is: 
    • has/have + been + past participle form of the verb.
    • Since the new subject 'the telephone wires' is plural, the auxiliary verb will also be plural.
    • So, 'has cut' changes to 'have been cut'.
  • At last line up the remaining part.
     

Following these steps, we finally get- The telephone wires have been cut.
